notes: • Refined app icon: dot, S and peak — the letters i-s-a as shapes.
• Wikipick remembers your reading position. Follow a link inside an article, then tap Back — the article you came from opens back up right where you left it, instead of jumping to the top.

• The language list is now honest: 21 languages plus "System", instead of a much longer list that quietly fell back to English for most of them. Pick one and every applet, dialog, and date follows it.

• The front door is a plain sentence about what this app is, not a wall of build numbers. A link to an applet that is not here now says so plainly and cleans up the address bar, instead of failing silently.
• Dispatch starts with a small example board (a few sample projects) instead of nothing, plus a "How it works" page explaining the basics.
• Wireframe opens straight onto its canvas now, instead of an extra screen you had to click through first.
• New Isa app icon — a navy coin with a carved-out i.

• Sketchpad — Icon Mode: turn any drawing into an app icon. Pick a platform template (macOS, Android, or favicon) to see the right guides overlaid on your canvas — macOS shows the rounded-squircle shape with an optional "Clip to squircle" toggle, Android shows its safe-zone circle and grid, favicon shows nested size squares — then export a full PNG size set, a macOS .icns, a Windows .ico, an SVG, a PDF, or "Export everything" as one zip with all of them.

• wikipick reader: following a link inside an article now opens that article at its own top, instead of landing wherever you had scrolled to on the previous one. Reader settings moved behind a "Reading options" disclosure, so a short window shows the article itself instead of one clipped line of text above the controls. An uncached link now opens a clean "Open this article?" prompt instead of a raw editing screen, and recently-read cards show the article title and language instead of a raw URL.

• Overflow menus and tab strips: the little arrow that reveals hidden items no longer sits on top of the item it is supposed to reveal, one tap now moves a useful distance across a crowded row instead of barely nudging it, and the ⋮ menu sheet no longer sits flush against the bottom edge on phones.

• Empty screens now have a button you can actually see. The main action on an empty list (like "Add applets") used to be almost invisible against the background — it is now a solid, high-contrast button, in both light and dark mode.
• Empty tables look finished instead of blank. A table with no rows now shows a centred icon and a short line of text, matching the empty panels lists and boards already had.

• Bublie follows dark mode. The board background used to stay pale blue even with dark mode on; it is now dark, and the floating menus you get when you hold a bubble (the style bar and link bar) are dark too, instead of a white panel over a dark board. Your bubbles keep their colours.
• The applet store is now on your home screen. A new "Applet store" tile sits beside your applets, so you no longer have to empty your home screen to find it.
• Every applet in the store now tells you what it does. All 65 applets have a one-line description, and three that described themselves wrongly have been corrected.
• No more spinner flash on quick screens. The loading indicator only appears if something actually takes a moment; fast screens just open.
• Home-screen tiles stand out in dark mode. Applet tiles are now their own slightly lighter cards rather than blending into the page.

• The app is now called Isa everywhere you see it — the launcher icon, home screen, menu headers, the About screen, and every share message. All internal storage, applet files, and the old links stay "isan" for now, so nothing breaks.

• New app identity: when you download and install Isa on Mac or Android, it installs as a fresh app beside any older "isan" version you have. Your old isan app stays untouched, with all its data. To keep your stuff, back it up in Settings → Backup or export it from any applet (Dispatch → project → Files → Export), then delete the old app when you're ready. The new app starts fresh — sign in to sync if you were signed in before.
• Get the app now shows the real publish date and time of each Mac and Android build, in your local timezone — so you know exactly when each version went live.

• Mac builds are unsigned. When you open Isa for the first time, your Mac will show a "can't verify the developer" message. Click "Open Anyway" and it will launch. (We're working on developer signing for a future version.)
• The download links changed: Mac is now isa-macos.zip, Android is isa-latest.apk. The old isan-macos.zip and isan-latest.apk links will still work for about 90 days, then they'll disappear.

• Fixed a bug where, at many common window widths, an applet with several tabs only showed the FIRST one — the rest were simply missing and unreachable. Wikipick, Taskly and every other multi-tab applet now show all of their tabs again at any width.

• Fixed a bug where opening a project or file could briefly show the WRONG one's contents, and where opening a project sometimes left no page selected so its canvas looked empty. Affects Bublie, Diagram, Docs, Notes, Sheets, Terrain, Taskly and Wireframe — each now opens straight to its own content, with a page auto-selected.
• Bublie's Outline view was mixing in rows from every board at once; it now shows only the board you are looking at, and scrolls properly when the list is long.
• Canvas text blocks are now readable in dark mode (they used to render in a color close to the dark background).
• Wireframe now supports multiple projects: a Projects tab to switch between them, soft-delete to a Trash you can restore from, and your existing wireframe work is carried forward automatically.
• New: an "Ecosystem data flow" map showing how isan's pieces connect, available both as a Wireframe project (4 pages, 7 toggleable layers) and as a Bublie board.

• Back now steps back INSIDE an app before it leaves it: if you moved from Today to Boards to Settings, Back walks you Settings → Boards → Today, and only leaves for the isa home screen once you are back on the screen you started on. Works the same whether you tap the arrow, swipe, or use your phone's or browser's Back button.
• Taskly's Settings (sharing, calendar files, current board) is now also one tap away from the ⋮ menu — look for "Agenda settings…" — instead of only being reachable from the left-side navigation.
